output.summary: An annual flowering herb native to Europe and western Asia, with a hollow upright stem and wind- or water-carried seeds. Young leaves are less bitter and can be eaten raw; leaves are also cooked, and steaming reduces the bitterness of older leaves.
output.edibilityNote: Leaves are eaten raw when young or cooked; steaming reduces older leaves’ bitterness. Young roots are also edible and used as a coffee substitute.
